05 — Example ​

Full, annotated implementation. Read it after kata submit 05 passes.

The compilable files are reference/ch05/agent/prompt.go and reference/ch05/agent/cmd/agent/main.go. The loop and the provider are unchanged from chapter 04, which is the point of the seam.

The shape ​

prompt.go   BasePrompt, Contributor, BuildSystemPrompt, AgentsFile
main.go     build the system message, prepend it to history
loop.go     untouched
provider    untouched

Two files changed. That is the design working.

Step 1 — the builder is a fold ​

go
func BuildSystemPrompt(ctx context.Context, base string, contributors ...Contributor) (string, error) {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString(strings.TrimRight(base, "\n"))
	b.WriteString("\n")

	for _, c := range contributors {
		if c == nil {
			continue
		}
		section, err := c.Contribute(ctx)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		section = strings.TrimSpace(section)
		if section == "" {
			continue
		}
		b.WriteString("\n")
		b.WriteString(section)
		b.WriteString("\n")
	}
	return b.String(), nil
}

Two details carry weight:

  • if c == nil { continue } lets a caller pass an optional contributor without a wrapper type.
  • if section == "" { continue } is where "nothing to add" is handled once, so no contributor has to think about spacing.

A contributor returns a section, not a line. It decides its own heading. That keeps the builder ignorant of what kinds of things contribute, which is what lets chapter 09 reuse it unchanged.

Step 2 — discovery walks up, rendering runs down ​

go
func (a *AgentsFile) discover() ([]string, error) {
	dir := abs            // the workspace
	var found []string
	for i := 0; i < depth; i++ {
		candidate := filepath.Join(dir, "AGENTS.md")
		if info, err := os.Stat(candidate); err == nil && !info.IsDir() {
			found = append(found, candidate)
		}
		parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
		if parent == dir {
			break
		}
		dir = parent
	}
	for i, j := 0, len(found)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
		found[i], found[j] = found[j], found[i]
	}
	return found, nil
}

The reverse is the whole chapter. Collected order is nearest-first, because that is the direction you can walk. Rendered order must be nearest-last, because that is the direction a model reads.

parent == dir is how the walk terminates at / without a special case. The depth bound is a second guard: a stray /AGENTS.md on a container image should not silently become project instructions.

Step 3 — empty is absent, and the heading is written once ​

go
for _, path := range files {
	body, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		continue
	}
	text := strings.TrimRight(string(body), "\n")
	if strings.TrimSpace(text) == "" {
		continue
	}
	if included == 0 {
		b.WriteString("# Project instructions\n")
	}
	included++
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n## %s\n%s\n", path, text)
}
if included == 0 {
	return "", nil
}

Three failure modes collapsed into one loop:

Without the guardWhat the model sees
no included counter# Project instructions with nothing under it
no empty check## /repo/AGENTS.md followed by a blank line
a read error treated as fatalthe agent refuses to run because one file was unreadable

A file that disappears between discovery and reading is skipped on purpose. The instruction is nice to have; the run is not.

Step 4 — the loop does not change ​

go
system, err := agent.BuildSystemPrompt(ctx, agent.BasePrompt,
	&agent.AgentsFile{Root: root},
)
history := []agent.Message{
	{Role: agent.RoleSystem, Content: system},
	{Role: agent.RoleUser, Content: *prompt},
}
res, err := agent.RunLoop(ctx, provider, tools, history, opts)

The system message is just the first element of history. RunLoop already sends whatever it is given, so nothing in the loop needed to learn about prompts.

That is worth pausing on. The instinct is to add a SystemPrompt field to LoopOptions and let the loop build it. That works and it couples the loop to prompt policy forever. Prepending a message keeps the loop's contract simple: it sends a conversation.

The diffs ​

1. Pasting instead of assembling — system-message-first

diff
- history := []Message{{Role: RoleUser, Content: prompt}}
+ history := []Message{{Role: RoleSystem, Content: system}, {Role: RoleUser, Content: prompt}}

2. Rendering in discovery order — agents-md-order

diff
- return found                     // nearest first
+ reverse(found); return found     // outermost first

3. A heading per file — empty-agents-md

diff
- b.WriteString("# Project instructions\n")    // outside the loop
+ if included == 0 { b.WriteString("# Project instructions\n") }

4. Unstable prefix — system-prompt-stable

diff
- fmt.Fprintf(&b, "# Context\nworking in %s at %s\n", dir, time.Now())
+ // nothing that varies between runs

Complete files ​

FileLinesWhat to read it for
reference/ch05/agent/prompt.go165the fold, discovery, empty handling
reference/ch05/agent/cmd/agent/main.go115prepending instead of threading a field

Comparison checklist ​

  • [ ] base prompt is a constant with no varying content
  • [ ] contributors are folded in order, nil and empty skipped
  • [ ] discovery walks up and is bounded
  • [ ] rendered order is outermost first
  • [ ] heading written once, only if something was included
  • [ ] unreadable and empty files skipped rather than fatal
  • [ ] system message prepended, loop unchanged
  • [ ] user message byte-identical to what was typed

Differences outside this list are style.
